description: Participants query relational data in SQL and check that the answers are right. In an embedded analytical engine on a laptop they move from keys and constraints through joins, grouping and common table expressions to window functions. They predict results before running queries, catch the silent errors that joins and NULLs cause, and test assistant-written SQL against known answers. The capstone answers a stakeholder brief on an unseen dataset.
audience: Beginners. Anyone starting technical data or AI work, including future analysts, data scientists, data engineers and AI engineers who can code but have not yet worked with messy real data.
prerequisites: Comfortable with spreadsheets: filters, sorting and simple formulas

outcomes.text: Explain the relational model: tables, keys, constraints, NULL and the grain of a table, given a six-table synthetic delivery schema
outcomes.evidence: an annotated schema with keys, cardinalities and grain matching the reference

outcomes.text: Identify the output of joins, grouping and NULL comparisons before running them, given small printed tables
outcomes.evidence: supervised AI-off check, eight of ten correct

outcomes.text: Write queries with filters, joins, grouping, subqueries and common table expressions that answer business questions, given a synthetic dataset of about a million order lines
outcomes.evidence: a query file passing the automatic checker on 16 of 20 questions

outcomes.text: Apply window functions to rank rows, compare periods and compute running and moving totals, given daily order tables
outcomes.evidence: queries matching reference outputs, each partition explained in a comment

outcomes.text: Implement a small schema with keys and constraints, load raw files into it and report rejected rows, given extracts with seeded defects
outcomes.evidence: a definition script and a load log accounting for every rejected row

outcomes.text: Identify silent errors in assistant-written SQL, such as join fan-out, wrong grain and missing business rules, given ten generated queries and a revenue rule documented outside the schema
outcomes.evidence: a verification note judging each query, with a test result
